title: How We Produced One of the Most Successful Crowdfunding Campaigns in History
titleZh: 我们如何打造史上最成功的众筹项目之一
bodyHtml:
In May 2022, Shenzhen-based battery manufacturer EcoFlow launched a new crowdfunding campaign for DELTA Pro, its most disruptive portable power solution to date.

The Kickstarter project just closed yesterday and DELTA Pro now ranks in the top 10 most successful crowdfunding campaigns in history. Behold, the final campaign stats:

  • 3,167 backers pledged more than $12 million
    • $1 million pledged in the first hour
    • $3 million pledged within the first day
  • Raised 12,080% of its $100,000 goal
  • Highlighted in Kickstarter’s Staff Picks from day one
  • Ranked 7th most funded project on Kickstarter

Our Strategic Approach to the Video

As Kickstarter asserts in their blog, “A video is by far the best way to get a feel for the emotions, motivations and character of a project. It’s a demonstration of effort and a good predictor of success.”

EcoFlow is no stranger to crowdfunding. They’re fully aware of the importance of video in the success of a campaign. So when they invited us to bid on the project, we knew we had to strategize a data-driven approach to the creative that would yield measurable results and meet their budget limitations.

Format & Style

All crowdfunding audiences want the same thing: detailed information. With this in mind, we opted for the traditional “product explainer” format but we didn’t want it to be just another Kickstarter video… DELTA Pro needed to stand out in the ocean of other projects as well as EcoFlow’s previous content.

We decided to use a combination of both live-action scenes and high-end 3D animation. This allowed us to visualize DELTA Pro’s more advanced features in a very clear and engaging way. While the live-action scenes provided relatable scenarios for target demographics, the flashy CGI helped elevate EcoFlow’s brand as a cutting-edge tech company.

Target Audience

From the start, DELTA Pro was set for a global release in virtually all major markets around the world. Its most important demographic would be middle-aged, tech-savvy families in the United States, so we knew we needed a Western look for our talent and locations.

We decided to film in Washington DC. It’s a rather uncommon shooting location that would keep costs low while providing plenty of options for a classic American-style family home.

This allowed us to achieve the look that EcoFlow needed for its key demographic. For Asian markets, our post-production team drafted multiple translations for the motion graphic text and voice over subtitles, so that the campaign would reach a wider global audience.

Deliverables

In this new era of digital marketing, repurposing content is more important than ever. For the DELTA Pro campaign, we wanted to make sure that EcoFlow had plenty of ancillary material for continued promotion over the next 6-12 months.

In addition to the main video, we provided three cut-downs for social media as well as key visual photos, which were shot alongside the video. Not only did this reduce the cost of each deliverable, it also gave all visuals across the campaign a cohesive look. Then, EcoFlow was armed with many months’ worth of content that could be shared across all marketing channels to drive more and more traffic to their Kickstarter page.

Budget Limitations

Our main strategy for achieving great results within the proposed budget was sharing resources between videos. In addition to DELTA Pro, EcoFlow planned to announce three other products at the same time. We put together a package for all four campaigns that greatly reduced the cost of each video by producing them together—with many of the same crew members, talent, locations, props, etc.

Shooting Internationally During COVID-19

The safety of our production crew is always a top priority so there was much deliberation over how we should manage an international shoot.

With the right preparations during pre-production, we were able to reduce our traveling crew to a single person. Our co-founder and in-house director, Zacharia Lorenz, flew from our offices in Vietnam to oversee the shoot while our producing team managed everything remotely from Asia. It was an ideal solution for minimizing potential exposure to the virus without hemorrhaging money toward travel costs.

We were also lucky to work with our friends over at LGND, who provided production support on the ground in Washington DC. We worked closely with LGND’s team to safely reduce the number of active crew members on set, keeping only the bare minimum that was required to achieve the creative.

Technology also played a huge role in this production. With one editor in the Philippines, one editor in Vietnam and a VFX team in Thailand, we couldn’t afford to waste days transcoding footage and shipping hard drives… Just two month before the shoot, Frame.io launched its new Camera to Cloud (C2C) real-time upload workflow and we were quick to jump aboard. With C2C, every time we wrapped a take, our video files would be instantaneously uploaded to our Frame.io library and transcoded. Within hours of wrapping each shoot day, all proxies were accessible to our multinational post team, ready to be downloaded and cut into something awesome.

And here it is… sit back and enjoy our director’s cut!

seo.metaDescriptionZh: Vantage Pictures 揭示了历史上最成功的众筹活动视频之一是如何从概念开发到全球发布的。

bodyHtmlZh:
2022 年 5 月，总部位于深圳的电池制造商正浩 EcoFlow 为迄今为止最具颠覆性的便携储能方案 DELTA Pro 发起了一场全新的众筹活动。

Kickstarter 项目昨天刚刚结束，DELTA Pro 现已跻身历史上最成功的十大众筹项目之列。请看，最终的活动统计数据：

  • 第一小时认捐 $1 百万美元
  • $100,000 的目标已筹得 12,080%
  • 从第一天起就在 Kickstarter 的 "员工精选 "中突出显示
  • 在 Kickstarter 上获得资金最多的项目中排名第七

我们的视频战略方针

正如 Kickstarter 在其博客中所强调的：“视频是感受一个项目情感、动机与特质的最佳方式。它展示了付出的努力，也是项目成败的有力预测指标。”

EcoFlow 对众筹并不陌生。他们充分认识到视频对活动成功的重要性。因此，当他们邀请我们竞标该项目时，我们知道我们必须制定一个以数据为导向的创意策略，既能产生可衡量的结果，又能满足他们的预算限制。

格式与风格

所有的众筹受众都想要同样的东西：详细信息。考虑到这一点，我们选择了传统的 “产品说明 ”形式，但我们不想让它成为另一个 Kickstarter 视频......DELTA Pro 需要在众多项目以及 EcoFlow 之前的内容中脱颖而出。

我们决定将实景拍摄与高端三维动画相结合。这使我们能够以非常清晰和引人入胜的方式将 DELTA Pro 更为先进的功能形象化。真人场景为目标人群提供了贴近生活的场景，而华丽的 CGI 则有助于提升 EcoFlow 作为尖端科技公司的品牌形象。

目标受众

从一开始，《DELTA Pro》就计划在全球所有主要市场发行。它最重要的受众群体将是美国精通技术的中年家庭，因此我们知道，我们的人才和拍摄地点都需要西方风格。

我们决定在华盛顿特区拍摄。这是一个相当少见的拍摄地，既能降低成本，又能为经典美式家庭住宅提供大量选择。

这样，我们就能实现 EcoFlow 针对其主要人群所需的外观。针对亚洲市场，我们的后期制作团队为动态图形文本和配音字幕起草了多个翻译版本，以便让更多的全球受众了解这项活动。

交付成果

在数字营销的新时代，内容的再利用比以往任何时候都更加重要。在 DELTA Pro 活动中，我们希望确保 EcoFlow 有大量的辅助材料，以便在未来 6-12 个月内继续推广。

除主视频外，我们还为社交媒体提供了三段剪辑，以及与视频同时拍摄的关键视觉照片。这不仅降低了每项交付的成本，还使整个活动的所有视觉效果具有凝聚力。这样，EcoFlow 就拥有了几个月的内容，可以在所有营销渠道分享，从而为他们的 Kickstarter 页面带来越来越多的流量。

预算限制

我们在预算范围内取得巨大成果的主要策略是在视频之间共享资源。除 DELTA Pro 外，EcoFlow 还计划同时发布其他三款产品。我们为所有四个宣传活动设计了一个套餐，通过共同制作大大降低了每个视频的成本--使用相同的工作人员、人才、场地、道具等。

在 COVID-19 期间进行国际拍摄

制作人员的安全始终是我们工作的重中之重，因此我们对如何管理国际拍摄进行了反复斟酌。

通过前期的正确准备，我们将出差人员减少到了一个人。我们的联合创始人兼内部导演 Zacharia Lorenz 从越南的办公室飞来监督拍摄，而我们的制作团队则在亚洲远程管理一切。这是一个理想的解决方案，既能最大限度地减少可能接触病毒的机会，又不会因差旅费而大出血。

We were also lucky to work with our friends over at LGND, who provided production support on the ground in Washington DC. We worked closely with LGND’s team to safely reduce the number of active crew members on set, keeping only the bare minimum that was required to achieve the creative.

Technology also played a huge role in this production. With one editor in the Philippines, one editor in Vietnam and a VFX team in Thailand, we couldn’t afford to waste days transcoding footage and shipping hard drives… Just two month before the shoot, Frame.io launched its new Camera to Cloud (C2C) real-time upload workflow and we were quick to jump aboard. With C2C, every time we wrapped a take, our video files would be instantaneously uploaded to our Frame.io library and transcoded. Within hours of wrapping each shoot day, all proxies were accessible to our multinational post team, ready to be downloaded and cut into something awesome.

就是这样......坐下来欣赏我们的导演剪辑版吧！

title: Vantage Pictures Taps into Inner Romance for OnePlus Y-Series TV Spot
titleZh: Vantage Pictures 在 OnePlus Y 系列电视广告中捕捉内心浪漫
bodyHtml:
Director Alexis Odiowei opens a window into a couple’s world. In this new commercial spot for the OnePlus Y-Series smart TV, we follow the journey of a young couple as they experience their first months living together.

In this new commercial spot for the OnePlus Y-Series smart TV, we follow the journey of a young couple as they experience their first months living together.

Director Alexis Odiowei wanted to break away from the conventional feature-based format & explore a more meaningful narrative that resonates with our emotional side. Alexis explains his inspiration for the core concept: “I saw the TV almost as a window into this couple’s world. We see the good, the bad & everything in between. At home, our TVs are often the focal point of the living room. So, I thought, why not switch things up and see these character’s lives from the TV’s perspective instead”.

Collaborating with OnePlus’ in-house marketing team, Vantage Pictures knew they had to develop something unique if they were going to capture the attention of consumers in a heavily saturated market dominated by big brands like LG, Samsung & Sony.

These little snapshots throughout the couple’s relationship felt like universal moments to which audiences of any cultural background could relate. However, focusing on such a ubiquitous story also came with its own challenges… The execution had to feel authentic & believable, as the subject matter is so familiar. The Vantage Pictures team carried out extensive casting in Cape Town, South Africa to find the perfect couple that would bring this story to life. The result was natural chemistry between the two lead characters that speaks for itself on screen.

title: Roborock Gives a Quirky Makeover to the Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
titleZh: Roborock 为无线吸尘器打造别具一格的新形象
bodyHtml:
Automated vacuum brand partners with Vantage Pictures on a series of short videos showcasing its latest cordless vacuum product.

Roborock, the design manufacturer behind its highly-rated robot vacuum cleaner S6 MaxV, has partnered with Vantage Pictures on a series of short videos showcasing its latest cordless vacuum product.

Produced to exhibit the new Roborock H7 cordless vacuum, the collection of six 15 second clips make vacuuming fun and amusing, emphasising the common cleaning issues we all face while explaining complex technological features with comedy.

“From the start we knew that creating an ad for this product would be a challenge because vacuum cleaner is a well-known category with little new to say,” said Andy Knight, global head of brand at Roborock. “To get around this we knew we had to take a different tact and create something that would entertain people rather than force specs on them as is the norm.”

A Fresh Twist on a Household Staple

The Roborock H7 cordless vacuum is a one-of-a-kind product leveraging advanced technology — and it features in a series of short videos made by Vantage Pictures that are just as unique.

“Our social media channels heavily emphasise humour and human connection, and we consistently receive stronger engagement on posts that aim more to entertain than to sell,” said Noad Auckburally, social media manager at Roborock. “With that in mind, we decided to go in the same direction for our commercials with the help of Vantage Pictures. Entertain first, educate second.”

The production company has enabled Roborock’s H7 vacuum to stand out in an intensely competitive market by highlighting key features in a direct and easily digestible way across six short videos, which were shot remotely over two days in Cape Town, South Africa

To convey the product’s lightweight yet powerful nature, Vantage Pictures filmed a short martial arts duel between masked assailants and a vacuum user, while use cases like cleaning animal fur are made equally compelling with chase scenes between a man masquerading as a dog and a vacuum-wielding homeowner.

Complex Technology, Simple Messaging

To highlight the powerful tech behind Roborock H7 vacuum, the production company relied on humour and exaggeration.

“The challenge was to take everyday chores, like cleaning your house, and give it a surreal twist. Projects that like this are always fun as they challenge us creatively and allow us to play around with the possibilities of commercial filmmaking,” director Alexis Odiowei noted.

For instance, the vacuum’s 90-minute battery life is explained with a car race-themed competition between a couple, complete with graphics for every “round” and a timer counting down the seconds.

By the same token, magnetism can be a dry subject but Vantage Pictures makes the product’s magnetic storage capabilities exciting in a quirky scene featuring a man covered in metallic objects.

bodyHtmlZh:
智能吸尘器品牌 Roborock 携手 Vantage Pictures，推出一系列短片展示其最新无线吸尘器产品。

Roborock 是备受好评的机器人真空吸尘器 S6 MaxV 的设计制造商，它与 Vantage Pictures 合作制作了一系列短片，展示其最新的无绳真空吸尘器产品。

为展示新款 Roborock H7 无绳真空吸尘器而制作的 6 个 15 秒短片集让吸尘变得有趣而好玩，强调了我们共同面临的清洁问题，同时用喜剧的方式解释了复杂的技术功能。

“从一开始，我们就知道为这款产品创作广告将是一个挑战，因为吸尘器是一个众所周知的类别，没有什么新意可言，”Roborock 公司全球品牌负责人 Andy Knight 说。“为了解决这个问题，我们知道我们必须采取不同的策略，创造出能够娱乐人们的东西，而不是像通常那样把规格强加给他们。”

家常菜的新花样

Roborock H7 无绳真空吸尘器是一款独一无二的产品，它采用了先进的技术--Vantage Pictures 制作的一系列视频短片中也有它的身影。

“Roborock 社交媒体经理 Noad Auckburally 说：”我们的社交媒体渠道非常强调幽默和人与人之间的联系，以娱乐而非销售为目的的帖子总是能获得更高的参与度。“考虑到这一点，我们决定在 Vantage Pictures 的帮助下，在我们的广告中也采用同样的方式。娱乐第一，教育第二。”

该制作公司在南非开普敦用两天时间远程拍摄了六段视频短片，以直接易懂的方式突出了 Roborock H7 真空吸尘器的主要功能，使其在竞争激烈的市场中脱颖而出。

为了传达该产品轻便而强大的特性，Vantage Pictures 拍摄了一段蒙面袭击者与真空吸尘器用户之间的武术对决短片，而在清洁动物皮毛等使用案例中，伪装成狗的人与挥舞着真空吸尘器的房主之间的追逐场面同样引人注目。

复杂的技术，简单的信息传递

为了突出 Roborock H7 真空吸尘器背后的强大技术，制作公司采用了幽默和夸张的手法。

“我们面临的挑战是将日常琐事，比如打扫房间，赋予超现实的色彩。导演 Alexis Odiowei 指出：”这样的项目总是很有趣，因为它们对我们提出了创造性的挑战，让我们能够发挥商业电影制作的可能性。

例如，这款真空吸尘器的 90 分钟电池续航时间是通过一对情侣之间以赛车为主题的比赛来解释的，每 “一轮 ”都有相应的图案，还有一个计时器在倒计时。

同样，磁性可能是一个枯燥的话题，但 Vantage Pictures 通过一个满身金属物品的人的奇特场景，使产品的磁性存储功能令人兴奋。

title: This Cross-Cultural OPPO Spot Delivers Much-Needed Nostalgia for Mother’s Day
titleZh: 这支跨文化 OPPO 广告为母亲节带来温馨怀旧感
bodyHtml:
In this new branded documentary for OPPO, we follow the children of the Bagasal family as they recreate special photos from their childhood to give mom a unique gift for Mother’s Day.

Creative director Alexis Odiowei tapped into a social media trend that has been popularised over the past few years, recreating photos from our childhood in the present day.

“I felt that utilising this trend would serve numerous purposes. First off, it would add an element of fun to the video, as often content centered around Mother’s Day is very sentimental and emotional,” he says. “We wanted to be a bit more lighthearted in our approach and the device of recreating childhood moments allowed the family to be more playful. Secondly, we wanted to show off the OPPO Reno7 Pro’s portrait mode. Showcasing old family photos side-by-side with the images taken on the OPPO Reno7 Pro illustrated the quality of the Portrait Mode feature in a natural way that ensured we didn’t have to call out specific features or take away from the story. Finally, we wanted to speak to OPPO’s target audience in a language that they understand. It seems every other month there is a new social media trend, this is a staple of the way in which Gen-Z audiences communicate with each other. Tapping into one of these trends allowed us to align the OPPO brand and their younger target demographics.”

On working with the Bagasal family, Alexis said: “It was important that we didn’t over produce or direct the family too much. Our approach was to simply give the family the mission and let them execute in a way that felt natural to them. To avoid doing multiple takes and breaking them out of their rhythm, we had two cameras rolling throughout. This allowed us to shoot long takes at different focal lengths, helping us maintain a natural flow throughout the day and avoid interrupting the whole process. The Bagasal family were so bubbly & fun and we felt the final film beautifully captured the real bond between mother and children.”

bodyHtmlZh:
在这部为 OPPO 拍摄的全新品牌纪录片中，我们将跟随 Bagasal 家族的孩子们重现童年时期的特别照片，为妈妈送上一份独特的母亲节礼物。

创意总监 Alexis Odiowei 利用过去几年在社交媒体上流行的趋势，将我们童年时的照片重现于今日。

“我觉得利用这一趋势可以达到很多目的。首先，它可以为视频增添趣味元素，因为围绕母亲节的内容往往非常感伤和情绪化，”他说。“我们想采用更轻松愉快的方式，而重现童年时光的装置可以让这个家庭更有趣。其次，我们想展示 OPPO Reno7 Pro 的人像模式。将家庭老照片与 OPPO Reno7 Pro 拍摄的照片并排展示，以一种自然的方式诠释了人像模式功能的品质，确保我们不必强调特定功能，也不会脱离故事情节。最后，我们希望用 OPPO 目标受众所能理解的语言与他们对话。似乎每隔一个月就会出现一种新的社交媒体趋势，这是新一代受众相互交流的主要方式。利用这些趋势之一，我们可以将 OPPO 品牌与他们的年轻目标人群结合起来”。”

谈到与 Bagasal 一家的合作，亚历克西斯说：“重要的是，我们没有过多地制作或指导这个家庭。我们的做法是将任务简单地交给一家人，让他们以自然的方式完成任务。为了避免多次拍摄，打破他们的节奏，我们在整个拍摄过程中使用了两台摄像机。这样我们就可以用不同的焦距拍摄长镜头，帮助我们在整个拍摄过程中保持自然流畅，避免打断整个拍摄过程。巴加萨尔一家非常活泼有趣，我们觉得最终的影片很好地捕捉到了母亲和孩子之间真实的亲情”。”

title: OnePlus 12 Campaign Celebrates a Bygone Era of Authentic Imagery
titleZh: OnePlus 12 广告致敬真实影像的黄金时代
bodyHtml:
Vantage Pictures and landscape photographer Joshua Cripps show what it takes to capture epic unaltered moon images with nothing but a smartphone.

With the recent explosion of generative AI, authenticity in visual content has all but deteriorated into nonexistence. Instagram filters, beautify apps, generative fill, text-to-image artwork… you can hardly browse a feed without scrolling past some deformed figure with perfect skin and thirty-eight fingers.

The AI revolution is inescapable and for many of us, especially in advertising, that’s all well and good. But last year, Samsung learned the hard way that we can’t just slap generative imaging into any application without public backlash… Since 2020, Samsung has touted the “Space Zoom” feature of its Galaxy cameras with incredibly detailed photos of the moon. After a few clever users debunked their claims of authenticity, Samsung was slammed by The Verge for misleading people when, in fact, the phones were utilizing AI to produce details that were never there in the first place.

So it seems brands will need to tread carefully as they continue to weave machine learning into the fabric of their products. Photographers, especially those with a passion for the natural world, take the authenticity of their work very seriously.

In the wake of Samsung’s fake moon fiasco, Chinese smartphone manufacturer OnePlus seized the opportunity to showcase the capabilities of its latest OnePlus 12 camera in a genuine #RealMoon campaign. Sporting 3x optical zoom and a 64MP sensor that enables up to 120x digital zoom with incredible detail retention, its new Hasselblad camera is a powerhouse for telephoto imaging.

Global production house Vantage Pictures teamed up with wilderness landscape photographer Joshua Cripps to produce a series of moon photos that would dazzle viewers with impressive detail never before seen from a smartphone camera—a brave endeavor on OnePlus’s part, no doubt. Cripps was free to make colour, contrast and exposure adjustments in Lightroom but under no circumstances could the images be composited or manipulated in Photoshop.

Meticulous Prep Work for Astrophotography

In honor of the tedious process required to capture unaltered lunar imagery, the team at Vantage Pictures proposed a longer-form behind the scenes documentary in addition to the 30-second spot. Executive Producer James Duong said, “We felt a single hero spot wouldn’t be enough to convey the core messaging. Because it wasn’t just about showcasing the end result of the camera specs. We wanted to celebrate the enormous workload that astrophotography demands, which is so easily undermined by digital manipulation.”

Behind the Scenes with Josh

Cripps and the production crew spent over three months testing prototypes, battling weather during short full moon intervals. OnePlus also wanted to include a human element, so the moon alone was not enough. Positioning a climber in front of the moon is no easy feat… Weeks of scouting, tracking lunar phases, calculating distance between subject and camera for various focal lengths—all of which needs to align at a precise moment so the sun illuminates the landscape without overexposing the sky. Not to mention the scant 20-minute window where the moon is low enough to remain in frame.

Stunning Results

The end result is a striking hero spot that blends anamorphic footage of Cripps in the field with enigmatic CG renders of particles coalescing into features of the moon. Shot in the Alabama Hills of eastern California, jagged granite spires produce an otherworldly look that beautifully supports the campaign’s extra-terrestrial theme.

Director Zacharia Lorenz said, “I was sweating bullets just days out from shooting. We were still wrestling with prototype bugs and deliberating locations, trying to piece together some semblance of a story that was unfolding into a logistical nightmare. But as soon as Josh took us out for a pre-scout, all the stars aligned. I was blown away by the location, our crew was small but nimble, and the obstacles we had to overcome really paved the way for a potent behind the scenes story. It was the kind of experience that reminds you to trust the process and find solace in the struggle.”

seo.metaDescriptionZh: 探索生成式人工智能和视觉真实性时代 OnePlus 12 广告宣传所面临的挑战。

bodyHtmlZh:
Vantage Pictures 与风光摄影师 Joshua Cripps 联手演示如何仅用智能手机拍摄震撼而未经修饰的月亮影像。

最近，随着人工智能生成技术的蓬勃发展，视觉内容的真实性已荡然无存。Instagram滤镜、美化应用、生成填充、文本到图像的艺术创作......在浏览新闻时，你很难不滚动经过一些拥有完美皮肤和38根手指的变形人物。

人工智能革命不可避免，对我们中的许多人来说，尤其是在广告业，这一切都很好。但去年，三星公司惨痛地认识到，我们不能在任何应用中加入生成式成像技术而不引起公众反感......自 2020 年以来，三星公司一直在利用其 Galaxy 相机的 “太空变焦 ”功能和令人难以置信的月球细节照片进行宣传。在一些聪明的用户揭穿其真实性之后，三星遭到 The Verge 的抨击，称其误导了人们，而事实上，这些手机是利用人工智能生成了原本不存在的细节。

因此，在继续将机器学习融入产品结构时，品牌似乎需要谨慎行事。摄影师，尤其是那些对自然世界充满热情的摄影师，非常重视作品的真实性。

在三星假月亮事件之后，中国智能手机制造商一加（OnePlus）抓住机会，在一场名副其实的 #RealMoon 活动中展示了其最新 OnePlus 12 相机的功能。新款哈苏相机拥有 3 倍光学变焦和 6400 万像素传感器，可实现高达 120 倍的数字变焦，并能保留令人难以置信的细节，是远摄成像的强力工具。

全球制作公司 Vantage Pictures 与荒野风光摄影师 Joshua Cripps 合作，拍摄了一系列月球照片，这些照片的细节让观众目不暇接，这是智能手机相机从未有过的，毫无疑问，这是 OnePlus 勇敢的尝试。Cripps 可以在 Lightroom 中自由调整色彩、对比度和曝光，但在任何情况下都不能在 Photoshop 中对图片进行合成或处理。

天体摄影的细致准备工作

为了纪念捕捉未经改动的月球图像所需的繁琐过程，Vantage Pictures 团队提议在 30 秒的广告片之外，再制作一部较长的幕后纪录片。执行制片人 James Duong 说：“我们认为一个单一的英雄广告不足以传达核心信息。因为这不仅仅是展示相机规格的最终结果。我们希望颂扬天体摄影所要求的巨大工作量，而这种工作量很容易被数字处理所破坏”。”

乔希的幕后故事

克里普斯和制作团队花了三个多月的时间测试原型，在短暂的满月期间与天气作斗争。OnePlus 还希望加入人类元素，因此仅有月亮是不够的。将登山者安置在月亮前并不是一件容易的事......需要数周的侦查、跟踪月相、计算拍摄对象与摄像机之间的距离以适应不同的焦距--所有这些都需要在一个精确的时刻对准，这样太阳才能照亮风景，同时又不会让天空曝光过度。更不用说还有 20 分钟的短暂空档，在这段时间里，月亮的位置足够低，可以保持在画面中。

令人惊叹的成果

最终的效果是将克里普斯在现场的变形镜头与粒子凝聚成月球特征的神秘 CG 渲染效果融合在一起，形成了一个引人注目的英雄广告片。在加利福尼亚东部的阿拉巴马山拍摄时，锯齿状的花岗岩尖顶产生了一种超凡脱俗的感觉，完美地烘托了广告的地外主题。

导演 Zacharia Lorenz 说：“在距离拍摄还有几天的时候，我已经汗流浃背了。我们还在与原型错误搏斗，斟酌拍摄地点，试图拼凑出一个故事的雏形，而这个故事的展开却成了一场后勤噩梦。但当乔希带我们去进行前期勘察时，所有的星星都对准了我们。拍摄地点让我大开眼界，我们的摄制组小而灵活，而我们必须克服的障碍也为一个精彩的幕后故事铺平了道路。这种经历提醒你要相信过程，在奋斗中寻找慰藉”。”

Each film centres on the simple idea that thinking outside the box can lead to significant rewards—a message that resonates with Bitget’s global user base. From creating a glamorous looking trip to Paris in your living room to turning a mundane Zoom meeting into a jet-ski adventure, the spots offer a fresh perspective on the world of crypto trading.

title: Bitget’s Humorous Human Moments Shake Up Crypto Trading
titleZh: Bitget 以幽默人性化瞬间颠覆加密交易
bodyHtml:
Vantage Pictures film director, Paul Boyer Moore, on infusing laughter into financial advertising and the joys of taking a work meeting from a jet ski.

Highlighting the profound effects of taking small smart steps, Bitget’s latest campaign, ‘Trade Smarter’, brings relatable moments and humour to financial advertising. To execute this, the cryptocurrency exchange and web3 company partnered with Vantage Pictures who produced a series of four films depicting comedic moments, where thinking outside the box transforms the ordinary into the extraordinary.

To delve behind the scenes on the campaign, LBB’s Sunna Coleman interviews film director, Paul Boyer Moore, who tells us how comedy can make an impact, how they came up with the funny scenarios and why he loves filming in Thailand.

What was the brief from the client and what initial ideas did you have?

Paul: Bitget came to Vantage Pictures with a pretty cool challenge: they wanted a series of films that highlight the importance of being smart in an amusing way, all tied back to trading smarter. The catch was that these films had to work across all target markets, including folks who are new to crypto trading.

So, we rolled up our sleeves and worked closely with the Bitget team to craft a concept that showcases real human moments where making a smart decision changes everything. That’s when ‘Smart Steps, Big Leaps’ was born – it just felt right. We brainstormed about 12 different ideas and, after some tough calls, narrowed it down to the four you’re seeing now.

The spots take a different approach than the usual financial / crypto trading ads. Tell us about the choice to use a humorous tone.

Paul: Financial ads can be so serious and, honestly, a bit dull. Bitget was brave enough to shake things up. Humour makes things memorable and relatable. When people laugh, they connect with the content on a personal level.

How did you come up with the different scenarios and select the final stories?

Paul: We tossed around a bunch of scenarios where everyday folks solve problems with clever ideas. One idea I loved was about a football fan struggling to watch a game due to two tall men blocking his view. Frustrated, he builds a huge throne of empty beer mugs to elevate himself so he can watch the game. It was so weird and absurd! We were so close to making that one. In the end, we chose stories that were more practical to shoot and would really resonate with Bitget’s audience.

Which spot is your personal favorite and why?

Paul: That’s a tough one, but I’d have to go with Mandatory Meeting. We’ve all been stuck in those endless, pointless Zoom calls, right? So when our guy decides to ditch it all for a jet ski adventure, it’s so absurd and unexpected. It still makes me laugh every time.

The spots were filmed in Bangkok – tell us about the locations chosen and any production challenges that came with it.

Paul: Filming in Bangkok was fantastic. It’s cost-effective and offers a wealth of international talent – actors who can really perform, not just stand there and look good. The western-style homes and beach locations also fit our needs perfectly for this global campaign.

One big challenge was our location move from a home film set to a beach jet ski scene. You’d think in Thailand that’s easy, but the nearest natural beach was two hours away, which didn’t fit our tight schedule. We got creative and found a man-made beach lake much closer. It saved us time and gave us better control without worrying about waves disrupting the shoot.

What was the casting process like?

Paul: Casting was a breeze. In Thailand, casting agencies really go the extra mile. They don’t just send audition tapes – they film entire scenes based on our storyboard, complete with makeup, wardrobe, props, and even edit it to music. It made it so much easier to visualise the final product and get the client’s approval.

What was the most enjoyable part of the production process for you?

Paul: Honestly, working with the actors was the highlight for me. Their energy and enthusiasm were incredible. They brought each character to life in ways that exceeded my expectations.

Anything else you’d like to share?

Paul: I just want to give a huge shoutout to everyone involved. Shooting four separate spots in four days was ambitious to say the least. But the collaboration between Bitget, the Vantage Pictures production team, and our amazing local crew at Triton made it all possible. Couldn’t have done it without them.

seo.metaDescriptionZh: 探索 Bitget 加密货币交易的商业广告，该广告以幽默和创意的方式突出智能交易，为金融广告注入活力。

bodyHtmlZh:
Vantage Pictures 导演 Paul Boyer Moore 谈如何为金融广告注入幽默，以及在水上摩托上开会的乐趣。

Bitget 的最新广告 ‘Trade Smarter ’强调了采取聪明的小步骤所产生的深远影响，为金融广告带来了贴近生活的幽默瞬间。为了实现这一目标，这家加密货币交易所和 Web3 公司与 Vantage Pictures 合作，后者制作了一系列四部影片，描述了跳出思维定势将平凡转化为非凡的喜剧时刻。

为了深入了解这次竞选的幕后故事，LBB 的 Sunna Coleman 采访了电影导演 Paul Boyer Moore，他告诉我们喜剧如何产生影响力、他们是如何想出搞笑场景的，以及他为什么喜欢在泰国拍摄。

客户的简报是什么？您最初有哪些想法？

保罗：Bitget 向 Vantage Pictures 提出了一个很棒的挑战：他们想要一系列用有趣的方式强调“聪明”这一点，并将其与更明智的交易联系起来的影片。难点在于这些影片必须能在所有目标市场中奏效，包括那些刚接触加密货币交易的人。

于是，我们撸起袖子，与Bitget团队密切合作，构思了一个能够展现真实人性时刻的概念，说明一个明智的决定可以改变一切。 ‘Smart Steps, Big Leaps’（睿智之步，飞跃之大）由此诞生——感觉很合适。我们集思广益，提出了大约12个不同的想法，经过一番艰难的抉择，最终精选出大家现在看到的这四个。

这些广告的风格与传统的金融/加密货币交易广告不同。请谈谈选择幽默基调的缘由。

保罗：金融广告总是那么严肃，说实话，有点乏味。Bitget 敢于打破常规。幽默能让人印象深刻，更容易产生共鸣。当人们笑的时候，他们会在个人层面上与内容产生联系。

你是如何构思不同的故事情节并最终选定最终的故事的？

保罗我们讨论了很多日常生活中人们用巧妙创意解决问题的场景。我喜欢的一个点子是，一个足球迷因为两个高个子挡住了他的视线而无法观看比赛。沮丧之余，他用空啤酒杯做了一个巨大的宝座，把自己垫高，这样就能看比赛了。这太奇怪、太荒诞了！我们差一点就能做出这样的故事了。最后，我们选择了更实用的故事进行拍摄，这样才能真正引起 Bitget 受众的共鸣。

你最喜欢的地点是哪里？为什么？

保罗：这很难选，但我还是会选“强制会议”。我们都曾被困在那些没完没了、毫无意义的Zoom会议里，对吧？所以当他决定抛下一切去玩水上摩托时，这太荒谬、太出乎意料了。每次想起来都觉得好笑。

广告片在曼谷拍摄--请介绍一下拍摄地点的选择以及制作过程中遇到的挑战。

保罗在曼谷拍摄非常棒。这里的成本效益高，国际人才济济--演员可以真正表演，而不仅仅是站在那里好看。这里的西式住宅和海滩外景也完全符合我们这次全球宣传活动的需要。

一个巨大的挑战是我们的拍摄地点从家庭电影场景转移到了海滩摩托艇场景。在泰国，你会觉得这很容易，但最近的天然海滩也要两个小时的车程，这不符合我们紧凑的日程安排。我们发挥创意，找到了一个更近的人工沙滩湖。这样既节省了时间，又能更好地控制拍摄，不用担心海浪会影响拍摄。

选角过程是怎样的？

保罗选角很容易。在泰国，选角机构真的是不遗余力。他们不只是寄来试镜带，还会根据我们的故事板拍摄整个场景，包括化妆、服装、道具，甚至还会根据音乐进行剪辑。这让我们更容易想象出最终产品并获得客户的认可。

在制作过程中，您最享受的部分是什么？

保罗：说实话，能和演员们一起工作是我最大的亮点。他们的精力和热情令人难以置信。他们将每个角色都演绎得活灵活现，超出了我的预期。

还有什么你想分享的吗？

Paul：我想向所有参与者致以崇高的敬意。在四天内拍摄四个不同的广告点，至少可以说是一个雄心勃勃的计划。但 Bitget、Vantage Pictures 制作团队以及我们在 Triton 的出色本地团队之间的合作使这一切成为可能。没有他们，这一切都不可能实现。

title: realme Unveils Humorous and Chaotic Spot for New 'Mishap Proof' C75
bodyHtml:
Vantage Pictures’ latest campaign displays the integrity of the realme C75 smartphone through placing the phone in a variety of relatable yet unfortunate scenarios.

Life’s full of surprises, and sometimes they’re chaotic. That’s where realme’s C75 comes in: aimed at on the go blue-collar workers. The commercial highlights the phone’s worry free waterproof, drop-proof, batter-proof features through hilarious mishaps.

Co-directed by Paul Moore and Zacharia Lorenz, they employed Phantom high-speed cameras and motion control rigs to capture the action. Slow-motion shots allowed them to showcase the character’s amusing reactions. “We put the C75 through the wringer! It handled anything from being run over by a motorbike to diving into boiling hotpot or spinning around in a washing machine!” said directors Paul Moore & Zacharia Lorenz.

The campaign, shot in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, by Vantage Pictures, was a cost-effective solution for the numerous locations required to tell these vignette-structured stories. Executive producer James Duong explains, “Vietnam has become the next advertising production hub of APAC with full-scale production at a fraction of the costs in many countries. Our production team in Ho Chi Minh City, proved to be a very efficient choice for the diverse locations needed to convey these stories. We were able to shoot the whole 60 second spot in just two days with numerous location moves and set builds.”

Matching the film’s lively tone, the music was composed by Two AM Music. “From the first briefing, we knew Paul & Zach meant business when it came to the music. The vocals had to lead the film’s message, so we all agreed to push for something addictively sticky. They gave us lots of creative freedom, so we went wild with vocal effects and deliveries.” says Oliver Stutz, audio director, Two AM Music.

The campaign is airing in markets across China, Indonesia, Vietnam, India, Mexico, Egypt, and Brazil.

title: MSI taps Vantage Pictures for its first global brand film in the B2B space
titleZh: 微星科技与 Vantage Pictures 合作，在 B2B 领域拍摄首部全球品牌宣传片
bodyHtml:
Vantage Pictures partners with MSI to produce its first global B2B brand film, showcasing business-ready solutions across retail, education, and SMB sectors.

When gaming hardware giant MSI officially entered the B2B market in 2020 with its “Business and Productivity” series, it marked a significant pivot for the Taiwan-based brand. But 2025 brought a new milestone: the launch of MSI Business’s first-ever brand film – a campaign aimed not just at selling specs, but at elevating how everyday professionals experience their work.

For that, MSI turned to Vantage Pictures, a global production company known for its extensive experience in the tech space. The brief: Develop a brand-forward film that showcases MSI’s expanding range of business PCs without leaning into the product-porn territory that’s so typical of tech. Instead, the focus was on aspirational storytelling across three key sectors: education, retail, and SMB (small-to-medium businesses).

“We knew we had to show the products in use, but we didn’t want to fall into the trap of making this feel like a spec sheet come to life,” says Zacharia Lorenz, co-founder of Vantage Pictures and director of the film. “MSI wanted something grounded, human, and relatable to virtually any market worldwide.”

The campaign consists of a 2.5-minute brand film “Elevate Everyday Work”, along with three 30-second cutdowns tailored to each sector. The story features a fashion entrepreneur in her boutique shop, a middle school teacher shaping young minds, and a cybersecurity analyst protecting critical infrastructure — each storyline subtly interwoven with MSI’s product ecosystem.

Undoubtedly, the biggest production challenge was time. From award to shoot, the team had just two weeks for creative development and pre-production. Scouting for real locations was off the table. Instead, Vantage leaned into Vietnam’s fast-moving art departments and cost-effective build options.

“Set builds are one of Vietnam’s secret weapons,” says Lorenz. “We had three large sets to construct in a single studio space, and our art director Jean Phan turned around visual mockups in under 24 hours. The sets were approved and constructed within just three days.”

The shoot itself was equally intense: 48 shots across two days, all in-studio in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Director of Photography Tóth Widamon Máté shot largely on steadicam to ensure fluid motion and rapid resets, adding production value without sacrificing speed. And with MSI’s team based in Taiwan, the shoot was entirely remote, with a live-streamed client monitor keeping things seamless across borders.

“Our goal was to create something that didn’t feel rooted in any one region,” Lorenz explains. “The casting, wardrobe, production design — everything had to feel international, while still being doable here in Vietnam.”

The final result is a sleek yet warm, human-centric brand film that communicates MSI’s business-to-business identity without losing the high-gloss confidence the brand is known for in its gaming line. It’s a strong signal that MSI isn’t just stepping into the business world — it’s moving with style and purpose.

seo.metaDescriptionZh: 探索引人入胜的MSI全球B2B品牌影片，它展示了在关键企业领域的创新和可靠性。

bodyHtmlZh:
Vantage Pictures 与微星合作，制作其首部全球 B2B 品牌宣传片，展示零售、教育和中小型企业领域的商务解决方案。

当游戏硬件巨头微星于2020年携其“商用与生产力”系列正式进军B2B市场时，标志着这家总部位于台湾的品牌发生了重大转变。但2025年迎来了一个新的里程碑：微星商用首部品牌影片的发布——这项活动旨在提升普通专业人士的工作体验，而不仅仅是推销产品规格。

为此，MSI 找到Vantage Pictures，这是一家以其在科技领域丰富的经验而闻名的全球制作公司。要求是：制作一部以品牌为导向的影片，展示 MSI 不断扩展的商用 PC 系列，同时避免像科技产品那样常见的“产品色情”风格。取而代之的是，影片将专注于教育、零售和中小企业这三个关键领域的励志故事。

“我们知道必须展示产品的使用场景，但我们不想落入俗套，让它看起来像是规格说明书的具象化，” Zacharia Lorenz说，他是 Vantage Pictures 的联合创始人兼本片导演。“MSI 希望它能接地气，有人情味，并且在全球几乎任何市场上都具有亲和力。”

此次宣传活动包含一部2.5分钟的品牌影片“Elevate Everyday Work”，以及三部针对不同行业的30秒短片。故事围绕着一位精品店里的时尚创业者、一位启迪学生心灵的中学教师和一位保护关键基础设施的网络安全分析师展开——每个故事线都巧妙地融入了MSI的产品生态系统。

毫无疑问，最大的制作挑战是时间。从获奖到拍摄，团队只有两周时间进行创意开发和前期制作。实地勘景的可能性被排除。相反，Vantage 公司依靠越南高效的艺术部门和具有成本效益的搭建方案。

“布景搭建是越南的秘密武器之一，”洛伦兹说道。“我们在同一个工作室空间里搭建了三个大型布景，我们的艺术总监让·潘在不到 24 小时内就完成了效果图。布景在短短三天内就获得了批准并搭建完成。”

拍摄本身同样高强度：两天内完成 48 个镜头，全部在越南胡志明市影棚内完成。摄影指导 Tóth Widamon Máté 大量使用斯坦尼康，以保证运镜流畅、快速重设机位，在不牺牲节奏的前提下提升制作质感。由于 MSI 团队远在台湾，整场拍摄完全远程协作，通过直播客户监视器实现跨境无缝沟通。

“我们的目标是创造一种不局限于任何一个地区的东西，”洛伦兹解释道。“选角、服装、美术设计——所有的一切都必须感觉是国际化的，同时又能在这里越南完成。”

最终的成果是一部造型时尚又不失温馨、以人为本的品牌影片，它在传达MSI的 B2B 定位的同时，并没有失去该品牌在其游戏系列中广为人知的耀眼自信。这发出了一个强烈的信号，表明MSI不仅仅是进入商用领域——它正以时尚和目标进军。

title: Vantage Pictures drops cinematic global campaign for OnePlus Pad 3 launch
titleZh: Vantage Pictures 为 OnePlus Pad 3 发布会投放电影级全球宣传广告
bodyHtml:
Vietnam-based production house Vantage Pictures has just released a visually striking global campaign for the new OnePlus Pad 3, showcasing the tablet as the go-to creative powerhouse for professionals who live and work on the move.

Shot entirely on location in Almaty, Kazakhstan, the film blends grounded storytelling with surreal visual metaphors—highlighting just how far the OnePlus Pad 3 pushes the boundaries of what a creative tablet can be. The decision to shoot in Kazakhstan wasn’t just for the dramatic mountain backdrops. “We needed access to a modern airport. We needed diversity in our cast. And we needed locations that didn’t look like a generic studio backlot,” says Paul Moore, Vantage Pictures Director. “Almaty gave us all of that—and more.”

The film follows three high-performance creatives—a game producer, an industrial designer, and a travel content creator—each unlocking their flow state using the Pad 3’s standout features. Scenes include cloning effects to visualize multitasking, stylus-drawn motorcycles that materialize into full-scale concept bikes, and airport lounges transformed into mobile editing bays.

Music and sound design was handled by Two AM Music. Kit Kuan Leong, Two AM Music’s Audio Director, said: “We designed the music and sound to echo the film’s central theme, clearing mental clutter and embracing ease. Each musical shift follows the characters’ journey, flowing seamlessly across moods while anchored by a simple motif. On the sound design side, we leaned into contrast: from the chaos of sensory overload to the crisp clarity of tech precision, letting every transition breathe and build with intention.”

The result? A fast-paced, premium-feeling, visually immersive spot that challenges conventional expectations of what a tablet campaign should look like—and reminds us that creativity isn’t limited by place, time, or tools.

bodyHtmlZh:
总部位于越南的制作公司 Vantage Pictures 刚刚为新款 OnePlus Pad 3 发布了一组极具视觉冲击力的全球广告，展示了这款平板电脑作为移动生活和工作的专业人士的创意动力。

这部电影完全在哈萨克斯坦阿拉木图实景拍摄，将具象化的叙事与超现实的视觉隐喻相结合——凸显了 OnePlus Pad 3 在创意平板电脑领域突破界限的程度。选择在哈萨克斯坦拍摄，不仅仅是为了戏剧性的山景。“我们需要现代化的机场。我们需要多样化的演员阵容。我们需要看起来不像普通摄影棚内景的拍摄地点，”Paul Moore，Vantage Pictures 导演说道。“阿拉木图给了我们所有这些，甚至更多。”

该影片讲述了一位游戏制作人、一位工业设计师和一位旅行内容创作者这三位高绩效创意人士的故事，他们利用 Pad 3 的出众功能解锁了他们的心流状态。场景包括用于可视化多任务处理的克隆效果，从中可以具象化出全尺寸概念自行车的触控笔绘制的摩托车，以及机场休息室转变为移动编辑室。

音乐和音效设计由Two AM Music负责。Two AM Music的音频总监Kit Kuan Leong表示：“我们设计的音乐和音效旨在呼应影片的核心主题，即扫除杂念，拥抱轻松。每一处音乐的转变都紧随角色的旅程，在简约的动机支撑下，在不同情绪间无缝过渡。在音效设计方面，我们尝试了对比：从感官过载的混乱到技术精准的清脆，让每一次过渡都能自然而然地、有目的地酝酿和发展。’

title: Confidence in every frame: Ulike taps Vantage Pictures for humorous beauty campaign
titleZh: 每一帧都充满自信：Ulike 借助 Vantage Pictures 开展幽默美容宣传活动
bodyHtml:
Ulike, a global beauty tech brand known for its at-home IPL (intense pulsed light) hair removal devices, has carved out a niche by helping women achieve salon-quality results—comfortably, conveniently, and pain-free. As the brand set its sights on the global market, it needed a campaign that went beyond features to speak to something deeper: confidence, intimacy, and self-empowerment.

To bring that message to life, Vantage Pictures, one of Southeast Asia’s most exciting production companies, stepped in to craft this direct to client campaign that was as bold as it was thoughtful. Directed by Alexis Odiowei and shot entirely in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, the four-film series fused situational comedy and emotional honesty to challenge traditional beauty advertising—and connect with women on their own terms.

“At its core, this campaign was about helping women feel confident in their own skin,” said Odiowei. “Whether in an intimate moment or at the beach, we wanted them to feel empowered—not pressured.” The creative team developed two “Leave the Lights On” films centered around women in private, empowering situations, and two comedy-driven spots that played up relatable, awkward moments—with Ulike’s device as the subtle confidence boost in each story.

Navigating a product in the personal care category demanded a careful tone. “We were dealing with something intimate, and didn’t want to alienate or patronize anyone,” said Odiowei. “So the storytelling had to be inclusive, humorous, but always respectful.” That mindset shaped everything from casting to art direction to wardrobe.

Custom-built sets reflected lived-in, realistic spaces—far from the typical sterile or idealized beauty settings. This authenticity was key to breaking beauty tropes and resonating with real women.

“Vietnam allowed us to stretch the budget while still achieving high-end execution,” said James Duong, Executive Producer at Vantage Pictures. “We built four detailed sets, sourced a diverse cast locally and from Bangkok, and worked with some of the best crews in the region.”

With more brands turning to Vietnam for high-end production solutions, Vantage Pictures is leading the way. “Every time we host a new client in Vietnam, they’re blown away by what’s possible here,” added Duong. “From infrastructure to talent, Vietnam is ready for the global stage.”

title: Director’s Brief: 12 Questions with Alexis Odiowei at Vantage Pictures
titleZh: 导演简介：12 个问题问 Vantage Pictures 的 Alexis Odiowei
bodyHtml:
Director’s Brief: 12 Questions is a new Q&A series from Campaign Brief Asia that shines a spotlight on the broad mix of talent shaping Asia’s commercial directing scene. Kicking off the series is Alexis Odiowei of Vantage Pictures.

1. Describe your directing style in one paragraph.

My directing style blends physical humour, uncanny situations and visually stimulating cinematography. I’m always trying to create little moments that make you chuckle while watching and hopefully leave a lasting impression.

2. Was there a specific ad that made you think, “I want to do this for a living”?

There was no one particular ad that made me think I wanted to do this for a living, but there’s lots of ads that stick in my mind when I think about what I love about advertising when it’s done well. Some of them are Tango – Orange Man Advert, Guinness – The Surfer, Cadburys – Gorilla, Sainsbury’s – 1914

3. What’s your all-time favourite TVC?

My all time favourite TVC is probably Guinness – The Surfer. I think it’s a visual masterpiece that powerfully captures the brand messaging and draws on themes of struggle, patience and triumph, making it not only incredibly memorable but also relatable. Many ads today are inspired by other ads but this commercial’s inspiration was art and literature.

4. What’s your all-time favourite TVC/Campaign from your country?

Well the Guinness ad is my favourite from my country. My favourite campaign from Asia is an ad that was produced for Lunar New Year in Vietnam for a local TV station. It is a great mix of traditional Vietnamese culture, contemporary dance and stunning imagery.

5. In your experience, what’s the secret to a smooth director-agency-client vibe?

I think trust is the secret to a smooth vibe among all the parties mentioned. When we have trust amongst all parties there is less second guessing and the creatives are allowed to do what they need to do to make something magical.

6. Where do you go (or what do you do) when you need to recharge your creative batteries?

This is very important for me as I am director, but also a production company owner so it’s sometimes hard to find time outside of the commercial production sphere. Downtime from directing doesn’t always equate to downtime from the industry, as I still have to be concerned with the day to day of my business. However, I try to make time for a few things to recharge creatively and also more generally. Creatively I embark on personal projects outside of the commercial sphere. I usually try to keep these projects small so they can be completed in a timely manner and it also takes me back to that DIY feeling early in my career of just shooting with friends.

I’m also an avid martial artist and have been engaged in some form of martial arts training since I was a child. My current passion is Brazilian Jiu Jitsu. I train 3-4 times a week and compete 2-3 times a year. This gives me another passion completely removed from directing that allows me to be artistic in a different way.

7. Ever had a happy accident on set that turned out to be a game-changer?

I think the best happy accident, or I guess stroke of luck I’ve had, was when shooting with a poodle. We had a shot where we crash zoom into the poodle after it has gotten a silly haircut. Somehow the dog just understood the comic timing and it tilted it’s head with a bemused expression on it’s face just as the crash zoom landed on it. It just fit perfectly with the emotion we were trying to create.

8. Is there a mentor or person who has had a big impact on your career?

My Uncle used to take me to the cinema a lot as a kid and I would just always be watching movies with him. So I would say he was the first person to really open my eyes to filmmaking.

9. What’s the next big thing in commercial filmmaking? Explain.

I think with the rise of AI I think there will be a return to real stories. I think audiences will want to see more human stories and there will be a big shift towards branded documentaries and maybe even some more long-form documentaries connected to brands.

10. If you could direct a dream ad for any brand, which brand would you choose?

I think over the years I might have been Nando’s biggest customer so I think a commercial for them would be one way of them paying me back for my patronage. Otherwise as a martial artist I would love to make a commercial for the UFC.

11. If you could give one tip to an aspiring TVC director, what would it be?

I would advise two things. One, try to become knowledgeable in a specific area of the industry. A lot of great directors come from other backgrounds. Whether it’s an art background, acting post-production or cinematography, this can really help inform the style of director you become. Two, just start directing whether it’s music videos for a friend or making a short film or whatever it might be.

bodyHtmlZh:
导演简报：12 个问题》是 Campaign Brief Asia 新推出的问答系列，聚焦于塑造亚洲商业导演舞台的各类人才。Vantage Pictures 的 Alexis Odiowei 是该系列的开篇人物。

1.用一个段落描述您的导演风格。

我的导演风格融合了肢体幽默、不可思议的情境和视觉刺激的电影拍摄。我一直在努力创造一些小瞬间，让你在观看的时候会心一笑，并希望给你留下深刻的印象。

2.是否有一个特定的广告让你觉得 “我想以此为生”？

没有一个特别的广告让我觉得我想以此为生，但当我想到我喜欢的广告中哪些做得好时，有很多广告会在我脑海中留下深刻印象。其中包括探戈--橙色人广告、健力士--冲浪者、嘉堡士--大猩猩、森斯伯里--1914。

3.您最喜欢的电视广告是什么？

我心目中最爱的电视广告大概是 Guinness 的 The Surfer。我觉得它是一部视觉杰作，有力地捕捉了品牌信息，并借由奋斗、耐心与胜利的主题，既令人难忘又十分有共鸣。如今许多广告是从别的广告里找灵感，但这支片子的灵感来自艺术与文学。

4.您最喜欢的国家电视广告/活动是什么？

Well the Guinness ad is my favourite from my country. My favourite campaign from Asia is an ad that was produced for Lunar New Year in Vietnam for a local TV station. It is a great mix of traditional Vietnamese culture, contemporary dance and stunning imagery.

5.根据您的经验，导演--经纪公司--客户之间和谐相处的秘诀是什么？

我认为，信任是所有各方之间保持顺畅氛围的秘诀。当各方都相互信任时，猜测就会减少，创意人员就可以做他们需要做的事情，创造出神奇的作品。

6.当你需要给创意电池充电时，你会去哪里（或做什么）？

这对我来说非常重要，因为我既是导演，也是制片公司的老板，所以有时很难在商业制片领域之外找到时间。从导演工作中抽出的时间并不总是等同于从行业中抽出的时间，因为我仍然需要关心我的日常业务。不过，我还是会尽量抽出时间做一些事情，为创作充电，同时也为自己充电。在创意方面，我会在商业领域之外开展个人项目。我通常会尽量保持这些项目的小型化，以便及时完成，这也让我回到了职业生涯早期与朋友一起拍摄的那种 DIY 感觉。

我还是一名狂热的武术家，从小就开始接受某种形式的武术训练。我目前最热衷的是巴西柔术。我每周训练 3-4 次，每年参加 2-3 次比赛。这给了我另一种完全不同于导演的激情，让我能以不同的方式进行艺术创作。

7.有没有在拍摄现场遇到过意外，结果却改变了游戏规则？

我觉得我遇到过的最好的意外，或者说是最幸运的一次，就是和一只贵宾犬一起拍摄的时候。我们有一个镜头，在狮子狗剪了一个愚蠢的发型后，我们把镜头拉近到它身上。不知怎么的，这只贵宾犬就理解了这个滑稽的时机，它歪着脑袋，脸上带着困惑的表情，就在这时，变焦镜头落在了它的身上。这与我们想要营造的情绪完美契合。

8.是否有对您的职业生涯产生重大影响的导师或人士？

我叔叔小时候经常带我去电影院，我总是和他一起看电影。他是第一个让我真正了解电影制作的人。

9.商业电影制作的下一个热点是什么？解释一下。

我认为，随着人工智能的兴起，真实故事将会回归。我认为观众会希望看到更多的人性故事，品牌纪录片将出现重大转变，甚至可能出现更多与品牌相关的长篇纪录片。

10.如果你能为任何品牌执导一则梦幻广告，你会选择哪个品牌？

我想多年来我可能一直是南多公司最大的客户，因此我认为为他们拍摄广告是他们回报我的一种方式。另外，作为一名武术家，我很想为终极格斗锦标赛（UFC）拍一个广告。

11.如果您能给有抱负的 TVC 导演一个建议，您会是什么？

我有两个建议。第一，努力学习行业内某一特定领域的知识。很多伟大的导演都有其他背景。无论是艺术背景、表演后期制作还是电影摄影，这都能真正帮助你形成自己的导演风格。其次，无论是为朋友拍摄音乐录影带，还是制作短片或其他任何形式的作品，都可以开始执导。

title: Govee’s haunted light show: Vantage Pictures turns Vietnam suburb into a horror film set
titleZh: 戈维的鬼魅灯光秀：Vantage Pictures 将越南郊区变成恐怖片场景
bodyHtml:
When smart lighting brand Govee approached Vantage Pictures with a Halloween brief, the idea was as eerie as it was illuminating – a campaign inspired by The Shining.

“Govee gave us a great starting point,” says Executive Producer James Duong. “We loved the play on words between shining and light — it connected perfectly to Govee’s core product. From there, we built it into a full campaign: one hero film and three short Alexa co-branded spots.”

Shot entirely in Phan Thiết, Vietnam the campaign’s suburban setting was meticulously art-directed to feel like small-town America.

“We looked at multiple cities in Vietnam — Ho Chi Minh City, Đà Lạt — and finally found the perfect neighbourhood in Phan Thiết,” added Duong. “The architecture and street layout gave us that American suburban feel, and we could light and control an entire block.”

Nearly two tons of Govee lighting hardware were incorporated into the house: in windows, props, and furniture, allowing the light to move naturally through the scene.

Director Salihin Ramli recalls the surreal energy on set. “The joy was in finding that sweet spot where light, fear, and laughter all collide. I had an incredible time working with a cast and crew who brought this hauntingly fun world to life.”

“Lighting a light product is tricky,” said Duong. “You have to make it look beautiful while it’s performing in the scene.”

To pull it off, the crew rigged a massive truss above the house, combining traditional fixtures with Govee’s smart lighting systems. Most of the scenes were lit primarily by the products themselves — deep purples, blues, and golds that blended seamlessly with cinematic light.

“It was like running a live concert,” Duong says. “We synced the Govee app to DMX controls, pre-programmed every cue, and synced it all to choreography. Once it started, everything — lights, camera, and performance — moved together in rhythm.”

Rather than rely on CGI, Vantage leaned heavily on practical effects: full prosthetic zombies, silicone bone textures, and makeup sessions lasting up to eight hours.

“It gave the film that tactile realism,” Duong says. “The hardest part was timing — syncing light cues with the dancers and effects. When it all hit perfectly, it was pure magic.”

“Vietnam offers the best of both worlds,” says Duong. “You can build big, shoot fast, and still keep it high quality. The local crews are incredible — technical, creative, and passionate. Everyone goes the extra mile.”

He believes this project showcases Vietnam’s rising reputation as a global production hub. “It proves we can execute large-scale lighting and practical effects at an international level,” he adds.

After three straight night shoots, the wrap was emotional. “Seeing the rough cuts on set and realizing it all worked — that was a huge moment,” Duong recalls. “Everyone brought something special,” he says. “Our lead actor Rory added humor and personality that made it all come alive.”

For Vantage Pictures, it’s not just a Halloween campaign — it’s a benchmark for what’s possible in Vietnam.

bodyHtmlZh:
当智能照明品牌 Govee 向 Vantage Pictures 提出万圣节活动的要求时，Vantage Pictures 的想法既阴森恐怖又充满照明效果--活动灵感来自《闪灵》。

“Govee 为我们提供了一个绝佳的起点，”执行制片人 James Duong说。“我们很喜欢”闪耀’和‘光’之间的文字游戏——它完美地契合了 Govee 的核心产品。从那时起，我们将其扩展为一个完整的活动：一部主影片以及三个与 Alexa 联合品牌的短片。”

本次广告大片全程在越南藩切拍摄，其郊区背景经过精心布置，旨在营造出美国小镇的感觉。

“我们在越南考察了多个城市——胡志明市、大叻——最终在藩切找到了完美的街区，”杨补充道。“这里的建筑和街道布局让我们感觉就像在美国郊区，而且我们可以照亮并控制整个街区。”

房子里安装了近两吨 Govee 照明硬件：在窗户、道具和家具中，让光线能够自然地穿过场景。

导演萨利欣·拉姆利回忆起片场那种超现实般的能量。“乐趣在于找到光影、恐惧和欢笑交织在一起的那个甜蜜点。与将这个令人毛骨悚然又充满乐趣的世界呈现在观众眼前的演员和剧组人员一起工作，我度过了一段非常愉快的时光。”

“照亮一个灯光产品很棘手，”Duong说。“你必须让它在场景中表演时看起来很美。”

要实现这一目标，剧组在家宅上方搭建了一个巨大的桁架，将传统灯具与Govee的智能照明系统相结合。大部分场景主要由产品本身进行布光——深紫色、蓝色和金色与电影光效无缝融合。

“这就像在举办一场现场演唱会，”Duong 表示。“我们将 Govee 应用与 DMX 控制同步，预先编程了每一个信号，并将其全部与编舞同步。一旦开始，所有东西——灯光、摄像机和表演——都随着节奏一起律动。”

与其依赖 C G I，Vantage 则大量采用了实景特效：逼真的假肢僵尸、硅胶骨骼纹理以及长达八小时的化妆过程。

“这赋予了电影那种触手可及的真实感，”Duong 说。“最难的部分是时机——将灯光提示与舞者和特效同步。当一切都完美契合时，那就是纯粹的魔法。”

“越南两全其美，”Duong说。“你可以大规模制作，快速拍摄，同时保持高质量。当地的摄制组非常棒——技术精湛，富有创意，充满热情。每个人都会付出额外的努力。”

他认为这个项目展示了越南作为全球制造中心日益增长的声誉。“这证明了我们可以达到国际水平，执行大型灯光和特效，”他补充道。

经过连续三晚的拍摄，杀青的场面十分感人。Duong回忆道：“在片场看到粗剪片段，意识到一切都奏效了——那是一个重要的时刻。”他说：“每个人都贡献了特别的东西。我们的首席演员罗里（Rory）加入了幽默和个性，让一切都鲜活起来。”

对于Vantage Pictures来说，这不仅仅是一个万圣节活动—— it’s a benchmark for what’s possible in Vietnam.

title: Vantage Pictures and realme turn nightlife into an AI-powered dream in “Live For Real” campaign
titleZh: Vantage Pictures 和 realme 在 “Live For Real ”活动中将夜生活变成人工智能驱动的梦想
bodyHtml:
When realme set out to launch its new 15 Series 5G, the brief was simple: make it feel alive. What emerged was Live For Real – a high-voltage night odyssey that pulses with energy, style, and movement. Produced by Vantage Pictures and directed by Guy Bolandi, the film transforms an ordinary night out into a dreamlike blend of AI magic and disco-era glamour.

At its heart, Live For Real follows a young woman as she leaves the office and steps into the night. One moment she’s waiting at a bus stop, the next she’s lost in music and light — her realme 15 capturing every beat of her journey.

“We wanted to show how AI can elevate real life — how technology makes the ordinary feel cinematic,” says Alexis Odiowei, Creative Director at Vantage Pictures.

That idea crystallizes in a striking sequence where her outfit morphs from workwear to nightlife chic — a vibrant reflection of the phone’s own AI-powered transformations.

“The film isn’t really set in any specific era,” Bolandi explains. “It lives somewhere between the ’70s and ’80s — that Studio 54 energy — with a modern touch. The lighting, the wardrobe, the camera movement… everything was inspired by that world.”

The location at Nu Boyana Studios in Bulgaria, with its New York City backlot, became the perfect stand-in for that golden-age nightlife. “Even the entrance looked like Studio 54,” Bolandi laughs. “Once we lit it, it came alive — shimmering, colorful, and full of motion.”

Finding the right performer was another stroke of luck. The lead — discovered by a production assistant.

Bolandi encouraged her to improvise, letting the camera capture real spontaneity. “My process is about trust,” he says. “You build an environment where the performer can just be. That’s when something authentic happens.”

The Live For Real campaign rolls out globally — across Southeast Asia, Eastern Europe, Russia, South America, and India — in multiple formats, from hero film to verticals.

“It’s a film about energy,” says Odiowei. “About stepping into the night and being your truest self. Whether you’re in Mumbai or Madrid, that feeling is the same.”

For Bolandi, the project was deeply personal — a chance to recreate the nightlife he’s always admired.

“I truly live and breathe those eras,” he reflects. “Studio 54, the ’70s, that New York pulse — all updated with a modern twist. Honestly, that’s the kind of world I’d want to live in. That’s how I see my parties.”

title: Director’s Brief: 12 Questions with Zacharia Lorenz at Vantage Pictures
titleZh: 导演简介：12 个问题问 Vantage Pictures 的 Zacharia Lorenz
bodyHtml:
Director’s Brief: 12 Questions is a new Q&A series from Campaign Brief Asia that shines a spotlight on the broad mix of talent shaping Asia’s commercial directing scene. The latest installment features Vantage Pictures director Zacharia Lorenz.

Describe your directing style in one paragraph.

My favorite projects are story-driven “documercials” and product launch films for tech brands, where we explore the human condition behind cutting-edge innovation. These two categories are stylistically different, so I don’t try to force a fixed approach—the tone and technique should always serve the brief.

That said, for most of my product work, I love getting weird with camera—mounting rigs in unexpected places, playing with macro probe lenses, and crafting dynamic sequences that feel like a rollercoaster ride through the product’s design and internals.

I also prefer slower, more intentional pacing when the concept allows. So many commercials rush to hold attention—understandable in the age of social—but there’s power in letting certain shots breathe. When clients are open to that rhythm, the work always feels more memorable to me.

Was there a specific ad that made you think, “I want to do this for a living”?

Not exactly. After uni, my sights were still set on working—commercials weren’t really on my radar. Then I got the opportunity to work at DJI in Shenzhen. As I was considering the idea of upending my life in the States, they released A New Perspective for the new Phantom 3 campaign.

Back then, drones were still new. People weren’t used to seeing mid-altitude aerials in that sweet spot—higher than a crane, lower than a helicopter. Today they’re so common, but at the time I was pretty blown away by it. The film captured this sense of exploration that really hit. It inspired the adventurer in me & pushed my decision to move overseas.

I’ve now been in Asia for over a decade. So in a way, the spot didn’t just influence my career, it reshaped my life. DJI opened the door to some unforgettable experiences and through that journey I realized commercial directing was where I wanted to be.

What’s your all-time favorite TVC?

“Favorite” depends on the day, honestly. But two spots come to mind—not just as inspiration, but as reflections of my own stylistic leanings.

First, Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Studio launch film. It nails everything I want in a tech product ad: clean, minimalist design; sleek motion control that pulls us through the product like a theme park ride; and seamlessly integrated macro CGI that reveals internal hardware in a way that’s both informative and mesmerizing. It’s fun to watch but still communicates key selling points clearly. The “Pure Imagination” cover was also a perfect music choice—emotive without being overbearing. I’ve referenced that film more times than I can count.

ASUS Zenbook’s “Incredible Comes From Within” is one of my favorite examples of a branded documercial done right. Reuben Wu’s surreal light-painting visuals speak for themselves. Anna Smoronova is a phenomenal DOP, balancing energy with space to breathe. You get chaotic close-ups, fast-cut FPV transitions, then suddenly you’re lingering on vast, cinematic wides. That emotional rhythm suits the thematic blend of innovation, nature, and craftsmanship perfectly. It doesn’t feel like an ad—it feels like a glimpse into something real. That’s always the tone I aim for in my own docu-style work.

What’s your all-time favorite TVC/Campaign from your country?

Off the top of my head, Spike Jonze never fails to inspire the filmmaker in me. I grew up on his films and music videos, and his commercials are just as memorable. Apple HomePod: Welcome Home and Kenzo World are pretty hard to beat.

I love that his spots don’t take themselves too seriously. They’re unpretentious and playful—you can tell the whole crew had a blast making them. It’s branded content, but it’s not pushing tech specs or some big message. He taps into the pure joy of entertainment—something all advertisers should keep in mind, even when the brief is product-heavy.

In your experience, what’s the secret to a smooth director-agency-client vibe?

Think like a contractor, not an artist.

As filmmakers, of course we want to create work that inspires us. But don’t get distracted by personal taste and lose sight of the brief. This ain’t the indie film business. As a commercial director, you’re hired to deliver a piece that fits the client’s brand and goals.

If an architect is hired to design a minimalist office, their client won’t be thrilled to receive a gaudy Art Deco mockup. Same goes for us. Do your research, analyze the brief, gather references, communicate clearly, and set expectations early. Don’t wait until the PPM to pitch your wild one-take idea that’s gonna clean house at Cannes Lions.

You’ll struggle to succeed if you’re tunnel-visioned by artistic ambition. Embrace the balancing act of collaboration…be creative, advocate for your decisions, but stay within the bounds of the brief.

What do you do when you need to recharge your creative batteries?

Cooking is a good reset for me. Meditative but creative. I get to work with my hands, follow a clear recipe, and have room to improvise. I love the rhythm of prep & the reward of sharing a meal with my girlfriend. Seeing her enjoy it is gratifying, like presenting a cut to a happy client. If I hadn’t gone into filmmaking, I probably would’ve pursued the culinary arts.

That, and video games. Huge nerd for open-world RPGs, survival sims, and strategy games. The hours I’ve spent on Bethesda titles, Cities: Skylines, and Civ VII… a lot. It’s how I unwind while still engaging that problem-solving part of the brain.

Ever had a happy accident on set that turned out to be a game-changer?

Can’t think of any accidents that turned out better than what we’d planned… but I have a fun story about the perils of prototypes & the importance of having the right support on set.

We’re in Iceland, shooting a launch film for DJI’s new industrial platform. We were documenting how Reykjavík search & rescue teams use drones in real-world emergencies. In a rush to meet our travel deadline, DJI’s engineers 3D printed plastic drone arms instead of the proper carbon fiber tubes.

We arrive at this tiny ramshackle S&R outpost in the middle of nowhere. We open the cases and, to my horror, the arms of every product snapped during the trip. Fortunately, our drone op was EU Creative Director Ferdinand Wolf, who’s not only a world-class pilot but an experienced engineer. By some miracle, he found an old broomstick with exactly the right diameter. He scavenged some rusty tools from the outpost, chopped it up, and reinforced the broken arms.

We shot four full days on a remote glacier, flying full-throttle with enterprise drones basically held together by splinters…didn’t have a single issue. We were on the brink of total failure but with Ferdi’s quick thinking and expertise, we returned with spectacular footage & a solid campaign.

Moral of the story: if you’re working with unreleased tech, always bring an engineer.

Is there a mentor or person who has had a big impact on your career?

Plenty of folks have influenced me over the years, but number one would have to be my high school film teacher, Aaron Passmore. He opened my eyes to the artistry of filmmaking beyond the Hollywood blockbusters I grew up on. Until then, my exposure to cinema was pretty limited—but in his class, we watched Kubrick, Hitchcock, Bergman, Kurosawa, Wong Kar-wai… and suddenly, I saw film as something far deeper than just entertainment.

His passion for the craft was infectious. He genuinely loved sharing it with his students, and that energy made a huge impression on me. I couldn’t wait to get to class—and often found myself skipping other periods just to sneak into the editing bay and learn more about FCP7. He made film feel like a world I wanted to live in, not just study from the outside. Looking back, his class was where the spark really caught fire.

What’s the next big thing in commercial filmmaking? Explain.

The cynic in me says AI will continue to dominate. As global markets expand, timelines shrink, and the demand for content accelerates, AI will become more pervasive—whether for streamlining workflows or generating visuals outright. The possibilities are exciting, but there’s a real risk of it dulling critical thinking and draining joy from the craft.

The romantic in me hopes the pendulum swings the other way—toward authenticity. As audiences grow weary of that soulless, artificial gloss of AI-gen content, they’ll start to crave real people having real experiences. Maybe brands will recognize this and reinvest in more live-action. Maybe AI gets so good that “real” becomes irrelevant.

If you could direct a dream ad for any brand, which brand would you choose?

The North Face, Patagonia, or Tompkins Conservation. I had a brief opportunity to work with Kristine Tompkins in southern Chile on a DJI Mavic Air spot, and I was deeply moved by everything she stands for. The ethos behind Doug Tompkins, Yvon Chouinard, and the fashion empires they built—not for excess, but to fund conservation & ecological restoration.

There’s purity in the way they’ve redirected success toward something greater than themselves. As an outdoor enthusiast, I can’t think of a more meaningful brand to collaborate with. Stories like theirs give me hope for humanity.

If you could give one tip to an aspiring TVC director, what would it be?

Don’t tie your self-worth to every job.

This industry moves fast. If you measure yourself by how “creative” or “cinematic” each commercial turns out, you’ll burn out or get bitter. You ain’t always get that dream brief. Sometimes it’s about craft. Sometimes it’s about client rapport & paying the bills. Either way, treat each project professionally and just leave the duds behind when they’re done.

You’re not being hired to prove your brilliance—you’re hired to solve problems, communicate clearly, and lead a team through creative complexity. That’s your real value. Ironically, the less you chase approval, the more trust you tend to earn.

Directing commercials is a long game. Build trust. Stay adaptable. Keep your ego in check. And save the passion projects for when your name’s number one on the call sheet.

What are your top 3 ads you’ve directed?

DJI Mavic 2 – Ski-Mountaineering with Jimmy Chin

This one’s more about the experience than the final product—though I still love the film, it’s not my best technical piece.

Working with Jimmy Chin was certainly a fanboy moment. I loved climbing & adventure sports growing up—so traversing the Greenland fjords for 9 days, bunking in a log cabin, scouting avi conditions, sending glaciers at sunset with some of the top ski-mountaineers…it was unforgettable. And a reminder of how much I love docu-style spots where we get to join technology, craftsmanship & natural beauty. The project had everything I care about: good people, wild locations, and a brand that trusted us to tell the story honestly.

OnePlus 12 – Chasing Luna

This campaign seemed doomed… right up until it wasn’t. Despite a tight budget, brutal timeline, and high-stakes technical objective, it ended up being one of my favorite documercial shoots.

We had to capture authentic astrophotography shots of the moon with the OnePlus 12—no AI, no Photoshop stitching. We shot two days in California’s Alabama Hills with photographer Joshua Cripps and a skeleton crew. A week before flying, it looked grim: bad weather, buggy prototype phones, and unusable test shots. But during the tech recce, the stars just aligned. Skies cleared, OnePlus’s team got us a firmware update, Josh mapped his shots, and my DOP Martin Buzora gave me loads of new ideas for scenes/coverage.

The final piece feels great & genuinely demonstrates the product’s capabilities in real-world conditions. Those are the wins that stick with you.

Bambu Lab X1 – The New Pioneer in 3D Printing

I like to learn something new on every project & this one gave me a chance to explore the world of 3D printing, something that’s always fascinated me.

It was my first time working with a motion control arm… “shooting robots with robots” as we liked to say on set. We aimed for that fast, rollercoaster vibe of my favorite Microsoft spots and I think we pulled it off well, especially on a much tighter budget. The CGI was a big hurdle, but the overall experience was a big step forward in my ability to illustrate complex tech with style.

bodyHtmlZh:
导演简报：12 个问题》是 Campaign Brief Asia 推出的一个新的问答系列，聚焦于塑造亚洲商业导演舞台的各类人才。最新一期的嘉宾是 Vantage Pictures 的导演 Zacharia Lorenz。

我指导的风格是协作和富有远见的，旨在为所有参与人员创造一个支持性的和鼓舞人心的环境。我重视开放的沟通和思想的交流，并努力赋予我的演员和工作人员在创作过程中发挥其独特才能和经验。我的目标是通过鼓励艺术家探索他们的潜在能力，并共同将一个共同的愿景变为现实，从而创造出深刻而难忘的表演。

我最喜欢的一些项目是故事驱动的“纪录片式广告”和科技品牌的发布会影片，在这些项目中，我们探索前沿创新背后的人性。这两类项目在风格上差异很大，所以我不会试图强行采用固定的方法——语调和技巧应始终为项目服务。

话虽如此，在我从事的大部分产品工作中，我喜欢用相机玩出花样——把摄像机架设在意想不到的地方，玩微距探测镜头，并创作出动感十足的序列，感觉就像坐过山车般穿越产品的设计和内部构造。

我也更喜欢缓慢、更具意图性的节奏，只要概念允许。许多广告为了吸引注意力而匆忙——在社交媒体时代这是可以理解的——但让某些镜头有喘息的空间是很有力量的。当客户愿意接受这种节奏时，这部作品给我的感觉总是更令人难忘。

有什么特定的广告让你觉得，“我想以此为生”？

Not exactly. After uni, my sights were still set on working—commercials weren’t really on my radar. Then I got the opportunity to work at DJI in Shenzhen. As I was considering the idea of upending my life in the States, they released A New Perspective for the new Phantom 3 campaign.

那时，无人机还很新。人们还不习惯看到那种恰到好处的中空航拍——比起重机高，比直升机低。如今它们如此普遍，但当时我对此印象极其深刻。电影捕捉到了一种探索感，着实打动了我。它激发了我内心的冒险精神，并促使我决定去海外发展。

我在亚洲已经待了十多年了。所以，在某种程度上，这个地方不仅影响了我的职业生涯，也重塑了我的生活。大疆为我打开了一些难忘经历的大门，并在这次旅程中，我意识到商业导演才是我真正想要从事的领域。

你最喜欢的电视广告是哪个？

“最喜欢的”说实话，取决于哪一天。但有两个地方能想到——不仅仅是作为灵感，而是我个人风格取向的反映。

首先是微软 Surface Laptop Studio 的发布影片。它精准地打到了我对科技产品广告的所有期待：干净极简的设计；流畅的运动控制，像主题乐园轨道一样把我们带进产品；还有无缝衔接的微距 CGI，以既有信息量又令人着迷的方式揭开内部硬件。它好看，但仍清楚传达卖点。“Pure Imagination”翻唱也是绝佳配乐选择——有情感却不喧宾夺主。我参考这部片子的次数多到数不清。

华硕 Zenbook 的《Incredible Comes From Within》是我最喜欢的“品牌纪录片式广告”范例之一。Reuben Wu 超现实的光绘影像本身就极具说服力。Anna Smoronova 作为摄影指导非常出色，在能量与留白之间拿捏得当。你会看到混乱的特写、快切的 FPV 转场，然后突然停在辽阔的电影感大远景上。这种情绪节奏与创新、自然与匠心的主题融合得恰到好处。它不像广告——更像瞥见某种真实的事物。这正是我在自己纪录风格作品里始终追求的调性。

您最喜欢的本国电视广告/宣传活动是哪个？

Off the top of my head, Spike Jonze never fails to inspire the filmmaker in me. I grew up on his films and music videos, and his commercials are just as memorable. Apple HomePod: Welcome Home and Kenzo World are pretty hard to beat.

我喜欢他的斑点并不那么认真。它们低调而有趣——你可以看出整个团队制作它们时玩得很开心。这是品牌内容，但它并没有推销技术规格或某个宏大信息。他触及了娱乐的纯粹乐趣——这是所有广告商都应该牢记的，即使在简介中产品很多的情况下也是如此。

在我看来，导演、代理公司和客户之间良好合作关系的秘诀是什么？

像承包商一样思考，而不是像艺术家。

作为电影制作人，我们当然想创造能激励我们的作品。但不要被个人品味所干扰，而忽略了简报。这里不是独立电影行业。作为一名商业导演，你被雇佣来交付一件符合客户品牌和目标的作品。

如果聘请建筑师设计极简主义办公室，客户收到浮夸的装饰艺术效果图肯定不会满意。我们也是如此。做足功课，分析简报，收集参考资料，清晰沟通，并及早设定预期。切勿等到 PPM（项目管理）会议才提出你那个能在戛纳国际创意节大获全胜的奇思妙想。

如果艺术野心让你固执己见，你将难以成功。拥抱协作的平衡之道……要富于创造力，坚持你的决定，但要遵循项目的宗旨。

当我需要为我的创造力充电时，我会做些什么

烹饪对我来说是一种很好的调适。既有冥想的成分，又富有创意。我能动手操作，遵循明确的食谱，同时也有即兴发挥的空间。我喜欢准备食物的节奏，以及与女友分享一顿饭的满足感。看到她享受美食，让我觉得欣慰，就像把一件作品呈现给一个满意的客户一样。如果我没有从事电影制作，我大概会投身于烹饪艺术。

还有，电子游戏。我非常痴迷于开放世界角色扮演游戏、生存模拟游戏和策略游戏。我在 Bethesda 的游戏、Cities: Skylines 和 Civ VII 上花了无数时间……非常多。这是我在放松的同时，还能调动解决问题的大脑部分的方式。

在片场有过什么意想不到的“快乐意外”，最终却改变了游戏规则吗？

想不出有什么意外比我们计划的更好……但我有一个关于原型设备风险以及在片场拥有正确支持重要性的有趣故事。

我们在冰岛拍摄大疆新款工业平台的宣传片。我们正在记录雷克雅未克搜救队如何在真实的紧急情况下使用无人机。为了赶上旅行截止日期，大疆的工程师们打印了塑料无人机臂，而不是使用了合适的碳纤维管。

我们抵达了这个偏远地区一个摇摇欲坠的搜索与救援前哨站。我们打开箱子，令我惊恐的是，所有产品的臂都因为旅途颠簸而断裂了。幸运的是，我们的无人机操作员是欧盟创意总监费迪南德·沃尔夫（Ferdinand Wolf），他不仅是世界级的飞行员，还是一位经验丰富的工程师。不知怎么的，他找到了一根直径恰到好处的旧扫帚柄。他从前哨站搜刮了一些生锈的工具，把它切开了，并加固了断裂的臂。

我们在偏远的冰川上拍摄了四个整天，驾驶着企业无人机全速飞行，它们基本上是用木屑粘合起来的……但没有出现任何问题。我们曾处于彻底失败的边缘，但凭借 Ferdi 的快速思考和专业知识，我们带回了精彩的素材和一项成功的宣传活动。

故事的寓意：如果你在使用未发布的尖端技术，一定要带上一位工程师。

是否有导师或对您的职业生涯产生重大影响的人？

多年来，有很多人影响了我，但排名第一的无疑是我的高中电影老师亚伦·帕斯莫尔 (Aaron Passmore)。他让我看到了好莱坞大片之外的电影艺术，而我从小看的都是这类电影。在那之前，我对电影的接触非常有限——但在他的课上，我们看了库布里克、希区柯克、伯格曼、黑泽明、王家卫…… 突然间，我发现电影远不止是娱乐，它还有更深邃的内涵。

他对这门手艺的热情极具感染力。他真心喜欢与学生分享，而这种能量对我产生了巨大的影响。我迫不及待地想去上课——甚至经常逃掉其他课程，偷偷溜进剪辑室，学习更多关于 FCP7 的知识。他让电影感觉就像一个我想置身其中的世界，而不仅仅是从外部去研究。回想起来，他的课才是我真正燃起激情的起点。

商业电影的下一个大事件是什么？请解释。

我骨子里的愤世嫉俗者认为，人工智能将继续占据主导地位。随着全球市场扩张、时间不断压缩，对内容的需求加速，人工智能将变得更加普遍——无论是用于简化工作流程还是直接生成视觉内容。这些可能性令人兴奋，但同时也存在削弱批判性思维和剥夺创作乐趣的真实风险。

我内心的浪漫主义者希望钟摆会转向另一个方向——走向真实。随着观众对人工智能生成内容的这种冰冷、虚假的“光鲜感”感到厌倦，他们将开始渴望真实的人们拥有真实的体验。也许品牌会认识到这一点，并重新投资于更多的真人场景。也许人工智能会变得如此出色，“真实”将变得无关紧要。

如果您能为某个品牌拍摄一部梦想中的广告，您会选择哪个品牌？

The North Face, Patagonia, or Tompkins Conservation. I had a brief opportunity to work with Kristine Tompkins in southern Chile on a DJI Mavic Air spot, and I was deeply moved by everything she stands for. The ethos behind Doug Tompkins, Yvon Chouinard, and the fashion empires they built—not for excess, but to fund conservation & ecological restoration.

他们将成功导向比自身更伟大目标的纯粹性令人钦佩。作为一名户外爱好者，我实在想不到有比这更具意义的品牌可以合作了。他们的故事让我对人类充满希望。

如果你能给一位有抱负的 TVC 导演一个建议，那会是什么？

不要把你的自我价值与每一份工作挂钩。

这个行业发展很快。如果你用“创意”或“电影感”来衡量每一支广告作品，你会筋疲力尽或变得愤世嫉俗。你并不总是能接到那个梦想中的项目。有时，这关乎手艺。有时，这关乎客户关系和支付账单。无论哪种情况，都要专业地对待每一个项目，完成后就把那些不成功的作品抛诸脑后。

您被雇佣来是为了解决问题，清晰沟通，并带领团队克服创意上的复杂性，而不是为了证明您的才华。这才是您真正的价值所在。讽刺的是，您越是不去追求认同，您往往越能赢得信任。

执导广告片是一场持久战。建立信任。保持适应性。控制你的自负。并将你的热情项目留到你的名字出现在点名单的首位时。

我执导的广告中，排名前三的是： 1. [广告名称 1] 2. [广告名称 2] 3. [广告名称 3]

大疆御 2 – 吉米·金的滑雪登山之旅

这次更多的是关于体验，而不是最终产品——尽管我仍然喜欢这部电影，但它并不是我技术上最好的作品。

与吉米·奇恩一起工作绝对是一个粉丝时刻。我从小就热爱攀岩和冒险运动——所以在格陵兰峡湾穿越了9天，住在一个小木屋里，侦察了雪崩条件，在日落时分与一些顶级滑雪登山者一起穿越冰川……这真是难忘。这提醒了我我多么喜欢纪录片风格的体育作品，在那里我们可以将技术、工艺和自然美景结合起来。这个项目拥有我所关心的一切：优秀的人、原始的地点，以及一个信任我们真实讲述故事的品牌。

一加 12 – 追逐月球

这项活动似乎注定要失败……直到它没有。尽管预算紧张、时间紧迫且技术目标风险很高，但它最终成为了我最喜欢的纪录片拍摄项目之一。

我们不得不使用一加 12 拍摄真实的月球天文摄影照片——没有人工智能，也没有 Photoshop 拼接。在加州的阿拉巴马山，我们与摄影师 Joshua Cripps 和少量工作人员一起拍摄了两天。出发前一周，情况看起来很糟糕：天气恶劣，原型手机有问题，拍摄的照片也无法使用。但在技术考察期间，一切都恰到好处了。天空放晴，一加团队给我们更新了固件，Josh 规划了他的拍摄，我的摄影总监 Martin Buzora 也给了我很多关于场景/覆盖的新想法。

最后的作品感觉很棒，并且真正展示了产品在真实世界中的能力。这些胜利会让你久久不能忘怀。

拓竹 X1 – 3D打印新先锋

我喜欢在每个项目中学习新东西，而这个项目让我有机会探索一直让我着迷的 3D 打印世界。

这是我第一次使用运动控制臂……就像我们在片场常说的，“用机器人射击机器人”。我们模仿了我最喜欢的微软广告那种快速、过山车般的劲头，而且我认为我们做得很好，尤其是在预算更紧张的情况下。CGI（电脑生成图像）是一个巨大的障碍，但总的来说，这次经历在我在艺术地展示复杂技术方面的能力上迈出了一大步。

title: Vantage Pictures delivers high-energy waterproof chaos in global campaign for the new realme C85 smartphone
titleZh: Vantage Pictures 在全新 realme C85 智能手机的全球宣传活动中提供高能防水混沌产品
bodyHtml:
With a playful superhero tone and the vibrant street culture of Vietnam, realme’s latest smartphone campaign by Vantage Pictures pushes durability and waterproofing to the extreme.

International production house Vantage Pictures has unveiled an exhilarating global launch film for the new realme C85 5G, a device positioned as the ultimate companion for young, hardworking users who spend their days outdoors. Shot entirely in Ho Chi Minh City, the spot highlights the C85’s durability, waterproof capabilities and long-lasting battery through a series of high-energy disaster-filled scenarios designed to push the phone to its limits.

Directed by Zacharia Lorenz, co-founder of Vantage Pictures, and shot by Singaporean cinematographer Kelvin Chew, the campaign taps into Southeast Asia’s working-class spirit while maintaining a premium cinematic feel. Set against the vibrant streets of Vietnam, from roadside eateries to narrow tube houses and the constant flow of motorbikes, the film captures the region’s unique rhythm and color, blended with English signage to keep it globally accessible.

“Our client wanted the phone to feel like a superhero, something that could take on anything,” says Lorenz. “So we leaned into a playful, self-aware tone for the voiceover, almost like a kid bragging on a playground. The phone talks big because it really can back it up.”

To emphasize waterproofing and durability, the team crafted a string of chaotic set pieces involving splashes, spills, storms and everyday work-site hazards. The visual language is fast, bold and kinetic, filled with dynamic camera movement, speed ramps and slow-motion liquid shots that heighten the sense of playful destruction.

Behind the scenes, the production leaned heavily into fast, flexible camera movement to keep pace with a packed two-day schedule. The team relied on Steadicam not only for smooth motion but also for speed, allowing them to move quickly between setups without time-consuming dolly tracks or jib rigs. Outdoor scenes were brought to life with full rain machines that soaked an entire Vietnamese street, creating controlled downpours that blended naturally with the city’s chaotic energy.

The tight production timeline also meant there was no opportunity for elaborate 3D animation. Everything had to be created in-camera, with only minimal VFX for cleanups and simple 2D enhancements. This approach placed even more weight on the practical effects team, who engineered custom liquid rigs to launch the phone into precise mid-air collisions with timed streams of water. These sequences were captured on a Phantom high-speed camera at 1000 FPS, resulting in dramatic slow-motion impacts that showcase the C85’s waterproof design with striking clarity. Pulling off this level of practical work on such a compressed schedule became one of the campaign’s biggest technical achievements.

“I wanted the film to feel energetic, fun and unapologetically messy,” Lorenz adds. “The C85 is built for people who work with their hands, mechanics, delivery riders, street vendors. We wanted to honor that world while elevating it with premium cinematography and stylized action.”

The client’s openness to showcasing Southeast Asian culture helped shape the aesthetic. Bustling street life, tiny plastic tables, smoky food stalls, busy local markets and the everyday grind of outdoor work become the backdrop for the phone’s heroic resilience. The result is a campaign that feels rooted, authentic and globally relatable.

bodyHtmlZh:
realme的最新智能手机广告由Vantage Pictures拍摄，以俏皮的超级英雄为基调，展现越南生机勃勃的街头文化，将耐用性和防水性推向极致。

国际制作公司 Vantage Pictures 为新款 realme C85 5G 推出了一部激动人心的全球发布影片。这款手机定位为专为户外辛勤工作的年轻用户打造的终极伴侣。影片全程在胡志明市拍摄，通过一系列充满高能量的灾难场景，将手机的耐用性、防水能力和超长电池续航能力推向极限，充分展现了 C85 的强大性能。

这部广告由 Vantage Pictures 联合创始人 Zacharia Lorenz 执导，新加坡摄影师 Kelvin Chew 掌镜。活动在保持高级电影质感的同时，切入东南亚工人阶级的精神气质。故事背景落在越南色彩鲜明的街巷——路边小馆、窄长的管屋，以及川流不息的摩托车——影像捕捉了当地独特的节奏与色彩，并混入英文标识，使其仍具全球可读性。

“我们的客户希望这款手机感觉像个超级英雄，什么都能应付，”Lorenz说。“所以我们采用了俏皮、自我意识的语调来配音，就像一个孩子在操场吹牛一样。这款手机说大话是有底气的。”

为了强调防水性和耐用性，团队创作了一系列混乱的场景，包括飞溅、泼洒、风暴以及日常的工地危险。视觉语言快速、大胆且充满动感，充满了动态的镜头运动、变速切换和慢动作液体拍摄，从而增强了充满乐趣的破坏感。

幕后制作人员大量运用了快速、灵活的摄影机运动，以跟上紧凑的两天拍摄日程。团队不仅依赖斯坦尼康（Steadicam）来实现平稳的运动，还依靠它来提高效率，从而能够快速地在不同布景之间切换，而无需耗时安装轨道车或摇臂。室外场景通过大型造雨机得以生动呈现，淋湿了整条越南街道，制造出可控的倾盆大雨，与城市混乱的活力自然地融为一体。

紧张的制作时间也意味着没有机会进行复杂的 3D 动画制作。所有内容都必须在相机内完成，只有极少的视觉特效用于清理和简单的 2D 增强。这种方法给实拍特效团队带来了更大的压力，他们设计了定制的液体装置，以精确地将手机发射到空中，与定时喷射的水流发生碰撞。这些场景使用 Phantom 高速摄像机以每秒 1000 帧的速度拍摄，产生了惊人的慢动作冲击效果，清晰地展示了 C85 的防水设计。在如此紧迫的时间内完成如此高水平的实拍工作，成为了此次活动最大的技术成就之一。

“我希望这部电影感觉充满活力、有趣且毫不掩饰地混乱，”洛伦兹补充道。“C85是为那些靠双手工作的人，比如机械师、送货员、街头小贩而打造的。我们希望在用高端的摄影和风格化的动作来提升他们世界的同时，也向他们的世界致敬。”

客户愿意展示东南亚文化，这有助于塑造了此次广告的整体美学。熙熙攘攘的街头生活、小小的塑料桌椅、烟雾缭绕的食摊、繁忙的当地市场以及户外工作的日常辛劳，都成为了这款手机顽强耐用、表现出色的背景。最终，这个广告系列给人一种根植于本地、真实可信且具有全球共鸣的感觉。

title: Bitget and Vantage Pictures launch campaign starring World Cup Champion Julián Álvarez
titleZh: Bitget 和 Vantage Pictures 推出由世界杯冠军胡利安-阿尔瓦雷斯（Julián Álvarez）主演的广告活动
bodyHtml:
Bitget, the world’s largest Universal Exchange (UEX), has launched a three-film campaign starring Julián Álvarez, fusing elite-level football with next-generation trading technology.

Created in collaboration with LALIGA and produced by Vantage Pictures, the campaign brings Bitget’s flagship products – Onchain, GetAgent, and Universal Exchange (UEX) – to life through Álvarez’s unmistakable on-pitch intensity. The films use Alvarez’s on-field precision, anticipation, and strategic timing as metaphors for how modern traders can navigate digital markets more effectively.

Directed by Paul Moore, the films were shot in Madrid, Spain under an extremely tight schedule: Álvarez was available for just four hours to capture all his shots. The team relied on extensive rehearsals with a stand-in, and a tightly engineered shot plan to ensure every take counted.
